notes: An athlete who did not start any trial or race is DNS; one who took trials keeps those results (Competition Rules, PDF p. 20).
Leaving the course or a technical infringement in a race is generally shown as DNF rather than DQ (Competition Rules guidance, PDF p. 20).

fully_automatic.ref: WA C1.1/C2.1 (2026), Technical Rules, Fully Automatic Timing and Photo Finish System (PDF p. 75)
fully_automatic.track_over_10000m: next longer 0.1 s unless the time ends in two zeroes (59:26.322 → 59:26.4)
fully_automatic.outside_stadium: next longer whole second unless the time ends in three zeroes (2:09:44.322 → 2:09:45)

hand.ref: WA C1.1/C2.1 (2026), Technical Rules, Hand Timing (PDF p. 73)
hand.outside_stadium: next longer whole second unless exact (2:09:44.3 → 2:09:45)

transponder.ref: WA C1.1/C2.1 (2026), Technical Rules, Transponder Timing (PDF p. 75–76)
transponder.all: next longer whole second unless the time ends in zero (2:09:44.3 → 2:09:45)

distance.ref: WA C1.1/C2.1 (2026), Technical Rules, Distance Measurement (jumps PDF p. 116, throws PDF p. 127)
distance.rule: record to the nearest 0.01 m below the distance measured if it is not a whole centimetre

wind.ref: WA C1.1/C2.1 (2026), Technical Rules, wind gauge reading (PDF p. 71)
wind.rule: metres per second rounded to the next higher tenth in the positive direction unless the second decimal is zero (+2.03 → +2.1; −2.03 → −2.0)
wind.record_limit_ref: WA C1.1/C2.1 (2026), Competition Rules, World Records (PDF p. 32): a performance with a wind average above 2 m/s in the direction of running is not ratified

track.ref: WA C1.1/C2.1 (2026), Technical Rules, Ties (PDF p. 83)
rules: If the judges cannot separate athletes for a place, it is a tie and stays a tie.

Tie for a ranking position or the last qualifying place by time: compare the actual times to 0.001 s; if still equal, the tie stays and lots decide (ranking) or tied athletes advance if lanes allow, otherwise lots.
Tie for the last qualifying place by place: tied athletes advance if lanes or positions allow, otherwise lots; this reduces the number qualifying on time.

field_horizontal_and_throws.rule: Equal best performances: the second best decides, then the third and so on; still equal → tie.

rules: 26.8.1 fewest jumps at the height last cleared;
26.8.2 then fewest failures in the whole competition up to and including that height;
26.8.3 then the same place, unless it is first place;
26.8.4 for first place, a jump-off (Rule 26.9) unless the competition decided otherwise in advance; not in Combined Events.

combined_events_scoring.ref: IAAF Scoring Tables for Combined Events (2016), Formulae (pages 22–23)

formula.track: P = a × (b − T)^c, T in seconds (e.g. 10.43)
formula.jumps: P = a × (M − b)^c, M in centimetres (e.g. 808)
formula.throws: P = a × (D − b)^c, D in metres (e.g. 16.69)
formula.rounding: round P down to a whole number

manual_time.rule: Hand times in events up to 400 m: add 0.24 s (below 400 m) or 0.14 s (400 m) to the time, or subtract it from b; no adjustment above 400 m.

notes: The pentathlon (men) uses the men's parameters of its events.
Compute with exact decimals (performance as recorded after rounding), then round down; floating-point results such as 998.9999999 must be treated with a tiny tolerance or decimal arithmetic.
